chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Did you inform anyone with what I informed you with?' I said, 'No, except for Suleyman ibn Khalid.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You have done well. Have you not heard the words of the poet: "Do not let my secret and your secret pass to a third! Indeed, every secret that exceeds two becomes common knowledge."'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on keeping secrets and sharing information?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates Ammar’s discretion by citing a poetic maxim that underscores the fragility of secrets when a third party is introduced. This narrative highlights the scholarly emphasis on *al-istikhfa'* (concealment) and the reliability of the *ahad* (single-chain) transmission within Shia hadith methodology, where trustworthiness is often verified through such practical tests of loyalty and secrecy.
